findings.title: updateEvent/deleteEvent look up destination calendar by externalId instead of credentialId, always yielding undefined
findings.body: In updateEvent (line 254-256) and deleteEvent (line 315-317), the fallback when externalCalendarId is not provided is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. Since externalCalendarId is falsy in that branch, `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` compares a string to undefined/null and can never match, so selectedCalendar/calendarId is always undefined and the code silently falls back to 'primary' (update) or 'primary' (delete). For collective events where the event lives on a non-primary calendar of a host, rescheduling or cancelling will update/delete the wrong calendar (or fail with 404 which is swallowed in deleteEvent). The lookup should match on `cal.credentialId === credentialId` (as createEvent correctly does at line 147-149) or the caller must always pass externalCalendarId.

findings.title: Google Meet fallback crashes when destinationCalendar is empty (undefined.integration)
findings.body: Line 118-119: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []; if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")`. When evt.destinationCalendar is an empty array (which many call sites now produce, e.g. handleCancelBooking, confirm.handler, requestReschedule.handler), mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and accessing `.integration` throws a TypeError, breaking event creation for any Google Meet booking that has no destination calendar configured. It should be `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

findings.title: Fallback path filters credentials by type === "calendar" which matches no real credential type
findings.body: In createAllCalendarEvents, the else branch (no destinationCalendar) does `this.calendarCredentials.filter((cred) => cred.type === "calendar")`. Credential types are app slugs like "google_calendar", "office365_calendar", "caldav_calendar" — none equals the literal "calendar" — so the fallback never creates any calendar event when destinationCalendar is empty. Previously the code relied on destinationCalendar being set; now that many call sites pass `[]` instead of null/undefined (e.g. bookingReminder.ts line 130, webhook.ts, confirm.handler.ts), bookings without a configured destination calendar will silently get no calendar event created. The fallback should use `cred.type.endsWith("_calendar")` (excluding "other_calendar" which is handled separately below) or pick the first calendar credential.

findings.title: createEvent called without externalId in the no-credentialId branch, losing per-destination calendar selection
findings.body: In createAllCalendarEvents, when a destination entry has no credentialId (line 375-382), the code calls `createEvent(c, event)` without passing `destination.externalId`. The CalendarManager.createEvent signature now accepts externalId and GoogleCalendarService.createEvent uses credentialId to find the matching destination calendar (`calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`). Without the externalId being threaded through, and since the destination entry lacks credentialId, the Google service cannot match the destination to the credential and falls back to "primary", so team hosts' events may be created on the wrong calendar. The call should be `createEvent(c, event, destination.externalId)`.

findings.title: Booking.destinationCalendar connect only persists the first destination calendar, dropping additional hosts' calendars
findings.body: The evt.destinationCalendar array is correctly built with the organizer's calendar plus all collective team members' calendars (teamDestinationCalendars pushed at line ~1074), and EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents creates calendar events on each host's calendar. However, when persisting the booking (line ~1871-1877), only `evt.destinationCalendar[0].id` is connected to the booking: `destinationCalendar: evt.destinationCalendar && evt.destinationCalendar.length > 0 ? { connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id } } : undefined`. The Booking model has a single destinationCalendar relation, so on reschedule/cancel the code reconstructs evt.destinationCalendar from booking.destinationCalendar (single) or user.destinationCalendar — the additional hosts' destination calendars are lost. Consequences: (1) reschedule/cancel flows (handleCancelBooking, EventManager.reschedule) will only update/delete events on the first host's calendar reference; other hosts' calendar events are updated only via booking.references (which do include all created references), but the destinationCalendar-based lookups in calendar services (e.g. GoogleCalendarService update/delete fallbacks) will target the wrong calendar; (2) the DB state no longer reflects which calendars the event was created on. This needs either a schema change (booking-to-destinationCalendar many-to-many) or at minimum ensuring all created references carry correct credentialId/externalCalendarId so updates/deletes don't depend on destinationCalendar.

findings.title: teamDestinationCalendars only collected for COLLECTIVE scheduling, but pushed for any isTeamEventType check that also matches ROUND_ROBIN incorrectly
findings.body: At line ~987-1000, team members' destination calendars are pushed into teamDestinationCalendars only when `eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE"`. At line ~1074, they are appended when `isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE"`. isTeamEventType was changed (line ~689) to `!!eventType.schedulingType && ["COLLECTIVE", "ROUND_ROBIN"].includes(eventType.schedulingType)`. For ROUND_ROBIN events, only one host is booked per slot, but the code path at line 1074 checks schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE" so ROUND_ROBIN is excluded from pushing — that part is consistent. However the deeper issue: for ROUND_ROBIN, `users` contains all hosts, and `users.slice(1)` team members are added to evt.team/attendees, and EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents will create calendar events for destinationCalendar entries — but for round robin only the booked host's calendar should receive the event. Since destinationCalendar for round robin only contains the organizer's calendar (eventType.destinationCalendar || organizerUser.destinationCalendar), only one event is created — OK. But the organizerUser for round robin is chosen per-slot; verify organizerUser.destinationCalendar corresponds to the actually booked host. If organizerUser is the event-type owner rather than the assigned host, the event lands on the wrong host's calendar. This needs verification; at minimum the collective-only gating means round-robin multi-calendar support is absent, which may be intended but should be confirmed against issue #7754.

findings.title: destinationCalendar set to null instead of [] when neither eventType nor organizer has one, inconsistent with other call sites
findings.body: Line ~1060-1064: `destinationCalendar: eventType.destinationCalendar ? [eventType.destinationCalendar] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [organizerUser.destinationCalendar] : null`. Other call sites in this PR use `[]` as the empty value (e.g. handleCancelBooking, confirm.handler, paypal-webhook). EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents checks `event.destinationCalendar && event.destinationCalendar.length > 0`, so null and [] behave the same there, but downstream code like `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` (EventManager line 118) handles both. The inconsistency itself is benign, but combined with the fallback bug (filter `cred.type === "calendar"` matching nothing), a null/[] destinationCalendar means NO calendar event is created at all for users without a configured destination calendar — a regression from the previous behavior where `eventType.destinationCalendar || organizerUser.destinationCalendar` being undefined still resulted in createAllCalendarEvents falling through to the (broken) fallback. Actually previously the fallback had the same `cred.type === "calendar"` bug? No — previously the else branch was only reached when destinationCalendar was falsy, and it had the same filter. So the regression risk is equal; the real issue is the fallback filter (reported separately). This finding is about consistency: use [] to match the type `DestinationCalendar[] | null` and other call sites.

findings.title: referencesToCreate externalCalendarId/credentialId now come from result, but createEvent's externalId param is destination.externalId while result.externalId is set from the same — verify consistency for non-Google providers
findings.body: In EventManager.create, referencesToCreate now uses `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId` (lines 169-170), which CalendarManager.createEvent populates from its new `externalId` parameter and `credential.id`. In createAllCalendarEvents, createEvent is called with `destination.externalId` only in the credentialId branch (line 370); in the else branch (line 380) it's called without externalId, so result.externalId is undefined and the created booking reference will have externalCalendarId undefined even though the event was created on destination.externalId's calendar (if the service honored it). For Google this is partially mitigated by credentialId matching, but for CalDAV (BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters calendars by mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId — the FIRST destination only) and Office365 (uses first destination's externalId), events for secondary hosts are created on the first host's calendar, and references record no externalCalendarId. This means updates/deletes for secondary hosts' events cannot locate the correct calendar. The else branch must pass destination.externalId.

findings.title: Lark createEvent throws when destinationCalendar is empty, breaking bookings without a destination calendar
findings.body: createEvent (line 128-132) does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId; if (!calendarId) { throw new Error("no calendar id"); }`. Previously the code was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` with the same throw, so behavior is unchanged for missing calendar — but now that many call sites pass `[]` instead of a populated object, and EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents calls createEvent for every destination entry AND for all "other_calendar" credentials unconditionally (line 399-405), a Lark "other_calendar" credential will throw whenever destinationCalendar is empty, causing Promise.all in createAllCalendarEvents to reject... actually createEvent in CalendarManager catches errors per-credential (line 236-254), so it logs and returns success=false. Still, for the primary destination path, an empty destinationCalendar array now reaches createEvent (via the else fallback branch which is broken anyway). The throw on missing calendarId is pre-existing behavior; the new risk is that `event.destinationCalendar ?? []` destructuring silently produces undefined and the error message is misleading. More importantly, updateEvent/deleteEvent have the same pattern. This is a pre-existing design (Lark requires a calendar id), so severity is medium: ensure callers don't invoke Lark createEvent without a destination calendar — EventManager's unconditional "other_calendar" loop (line 399-405) does exactly that.

findings.title: Unconditional creation of "other_calendar" events ignores destinationCalendar and can create duplicate/wrong events for collective bookings
findings.body: At the end of createAllCalendarEvents (lines 398-405), the code unconditionally creates events for all credentials whose type includes "other_calendar" (e.g. CRM pseudo-calendars like closecom_other_calendar), regardless of destinationCalendar. For collective events with multiple hosts, each host's EventManager instance... actually EventManager is constructed per-user (organizer), so this runs once. But the destinationCalendar loop (lines 338-383) iterates over ALL destination calendars (organizer + team members) and for entries without credentialId it creates events on ALL credentials matching destination.integration — meaning for a collective event with 2 hosts each having google_calendar, if the destination entries lack credentialId, events are created on both hosts' Google calendars for each destination entry, potentially creating duplicates (2 destinations × 2 credentials = 4 events, when 2 are expected). The destination entries built in handleNewBooking come from Prisma DestinationCalendar objects which DO have credentialId? DestinationCalendar model has credentialId? Let me check: the Prisma DestinationCalendar has `credentialId Int?` — in handleNewBooking, teamDestinationCalendars are user.destinationCalendar objects which include credentialId if set. If users set destinationCalendar without credentialId (possible?), the else branch creates events on all matching credentials — for collective with 2 google hosts, destination[0] (organizer, no credentialId) → creates on both hosts' google credentials; destination[1] (member, no credentialId) → creates on both again → 4 events. This is a real duplication risk when credentialId is absent on destination entries.

findings.title: Recurring-event cancellation deletes events using ALL of the booking user's calendar credentials instead of the reference's credential
findings.body: In the recurring + allRemainingBookings branch (lines 444-468), for each calendar credential of `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` (ALL calendar credentials of the organizer, not the credential that owns the reference), the code iterates updatedBookings and deletes the first `_calendar` reference found (`updBooking.references.find(...)`) using that credential's calendar service. For collective events where the reference belongs to a different host's credential, `calendar?.deleteEvent(uid, evt, externalCalendarId)` is called with the wrong credential — the externalCalendarId belongs to another user's calendar, so deletion will 404 (silently resolved in Google deleteEvent) or delete nothing. The outer loop already has the correct `calendarCredential` for the reference (line 428-441); the inner recurring loop should use that same credential/calendar, not re-iterate all user credentials. This leaves stale events on secondary hosts' calendars when cancelling recurring collective bookings.

findings.title: Cancellation evt.destinationCalendar only includes booking/user destination calendar, not team hosts' calendars
findings.body: When building evt for cancellation (lines 251-255), destinationCalendar is `[bookingToDelete.destinationCalendar]` or `[bookingToDelete.user.destinationCalendar]` — a single calendar. For collective events with multiple hosts, the calendar services' deleteEvent fallback (`event.destinationCalendar?.find(...)`) uses this array; since booking.destinationCalendar only stores the first destination (see handleNewBooking connect), secondary hosts' calendars are not represented. However, deletion primarily uses `externalCalendarId` from the reference (passed explicitly), so the impact is limited to the fallback paths in GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent (line 315-317) which are broken anyway (see separate finding). Still, for correctness the evt should include all destination calendars of the team members, or the deletion logic should rely solely on references (which it mostly does via bookingCalendarReference loop). The current code does iterate all references (line 422-483), so deletion per-reference is attempted; the evt.destinationCalendar is only used as fallback. Medium severity because the broken fallback in Google service makes this matter.

findings.title: destinationCalendar fallback to user.destinationCalendar was removed, and the original code was self-referential (bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar)
findings.body: The diff shows the old code was `destinationCalendar: bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar` (a self-OR, clearly a pre-existing bug — probably meant `bookingToReschedule?.user?.destinationCalendar`). The new code is `bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar ? [bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar] : []`. The booking query (line 43-74) does not select `user.destinationCalendar`, so the user fallback is impossible here without a query change. The evt is used for webhooks (BOOKING_CANCELLED payload) — the webhook payload's destinationCalendar will now be [] when the booking has no destinationCalendar, whereas other handlers (handleCancelBooking) fall back to user.destinationCalendar. This changes the webhook payload contract for consumers. Either include user.destinationCalendar in the query and fall back, or accept the change deliberately. Also note the webhook.e2e.ts test expects `destinationCalendar: []` for BOOKING_REJECTED and `null` for BOOKING_CREATED/BOOKING_REQUESTED — the null expectations at lines 119 and 373 were NOT updated (only line 249 was changed to []), meaning those tests will now fail because the payload will contain [] not null. Wait — line 119 `destinationCalendar: null` and line 373 `destinationCalendar: null` remain unchanged in the test file. The actual payloads: BOOKING_CREATED comes from handleNewBooking where destinationCalendar is now an array (possibly [] or [cal]) — never null. So `toMatchObject({ destinationCalendar: null })` will fail. This is a test gap/bug.

findings.title: BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED webhook tests still expect destinationCalendar: null but the payload is now an array
findings.body: The PR changed the CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar type to an array and updated the BOOKING_REJECTED expectation (line 249) from null to [], but left `destinationCalendar: null` at line 119 (BOOKING_CREATED) and line 373 (BOOKING_REQUESTED). The webhook payload is built from the CalendarEvent, where destinationCalendar is now always an array (e.g. handleNewBooking sets `[eventType.destinationCalendar]` or `[organizerUser.destinationCalendar]` or null — actually handleNewBooking can set null at line ~1064). Hmm, handleNewBooking sets `destinationCalendar: ... : null` — so BOOKING_CREATED payload could be null if neither eventType nor organizer has a destination calendar. In the e2e test, the user is created via fixtures — does the fixture user have a destinationCalendar? Typically not by default. So the payload would be null for BOOKING_CREATED (matching the test), but for BOOKING_REJECTED (confirm.handler) the code now always produces an array ([]), hence the test update at line 249. For BOOKING_REQUESTED — which handler produces it? handleNewBooking with requiresConfirmation — same evt as BOOKING_CREATED, so null is still expected and correct. So lines 119 and 373 may still pass. BUT the inconsistency: handleNewBooking produces null while confirm.handler produces [] for the same conceptual field — the webhook contract is now inconsistent across trigger events (null vs []). This is an API contract break for webhook consumers. The type is `DestinationCalendar[] | null` so both are valid, but consumers must handle both. This should be standardized to always [] (or always null) — recommend making handleNewBooking produce [] instead of null.

findings.title: Inconsistent empty value for destinationCalendar (null vs []) across webhook payloads breaks consumer contract
findings.body: handleNewBooking sets `destinationCalendar: ... : null` when no calendar is configured (line ~1063), while confirm.handler, handleCancelBooking, bookingReminder, and the payment webhooks all use `[]`. The CalendarEvent type allows both (`DestinationCalendar[] | null`), but webhook consumers receive BOOKING_CREATED/BOOKING_REQUESTED payloads with `destinationCalendar: null` and BOOKING_REJECTED/BOOKING_CANCELLED payloads with `destinationCalendar: []`. This is an inconsistent API contract introduced by the PR. Standardize on `[]` (matching the new array type semantics) in handleNewBooking.

findings.title: Calendar.createEvent interface now requires credentialId, but not all Calendar implementations were updated (CalDAV/BaseCalendarService, Office365, Lark)
findings.body: The `Calendar` interface in packages/types/Calendar.d.ts (line 221) was changed to `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number): Promise<NewCalendarEventType>`. CalendarManager.createEvent now calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` (line 236). However, the implementations in packages/lib/CalendarService.ts (BaseCalendarService.createEvent, line 125: `async createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)`), packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts (line 72: `async createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)`), and packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts (line 125: `async createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)`) were NOT updated to accept credentialId. TypeScript structural typing allows implementations with fewer parameters, so this compiles, but at runtime `credentialId` is simply ignored by these services — they always use the first destination calendar (BaseCalendarService line 156, Office365 line 73, Lark line 128). For collective events with hosts on CalDAV/Office365/Lark, events will be created on the wrong host's calendar (the first destination's calendar) because these services cannot select the calendar matching the credential. This defeats the PR's purpose for non-Google providers. Each service should accept credentialId and use `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` like GoogleCalendarService does.

findings.title: Office365 createEvent ignores credentialId and always uses the first destination calendar, breaking collective events
findings.body: Office365CalendarService.createEvent (line 72-92) only reads `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and uses its externalId. It does not receive or use credentialId (the interface change added credentialId but this implementation wasn't updated). In a collective event with two Office365 hosts, EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents calls createEvent once per destination with the corresponding credential, but the service always picks destinationCalendar[0].externalId — the organizer's calendar — so the second host's event is created on the organizer's calendar using the second host's credential (which will fail with 403/404 since the credential doesn't own that calendar), or if it succeeds it's on the wrong calendar. The service must accept credentialId and select `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, falling back to the first entry or the default calendar.

findings.title: BaseCalendarService (CalDAV/Apple) createEvent uses only the first destination calendar, ignoring which credential is being used
findings.body: BaseCalendarService.createEvent (line 125-198) destructures `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` (line 156) and filters calendars by that single externalId. It does not accept credentialId (signature unchanged at line 125). For collective events with multiple CalDAV hosts, EventManager calls createEvent once per host credential, but each call creates the event on the FIRST destination's calendar URL using each host's own credentials/headers — the second host's credentials will fail to write to the first host's CalDAV calendar (auth error), or worse, if calendars are shared, create duplicates. The service must accept credentialId and select the destination calendar whose credentialId matches, like GoogleCalendarService does.

findings.title: updateAllCalendarEvents: updateEvent called with possibly-undefined credential when DB lookup fails
findings.body: In updateAllCalendarEvents, when `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is neither in this.calendarCredentials nor found in the DB (credentialFromDB null or app.slug missing), `credential` remains undefined (or retains the value from a previous loop iteration — it's declared with `let credential;` outside the try and reused across iterations of the for loop at line 504!). Then `result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId))` is called with undefined credential. updateEvent (CalendarManager line 272) does `getCalendar(credential)` with undefined — likely throws, caught by the outer try/catch which returns failure results. But worse: `credential` is declared outside the for loop (line 480: `let calendarReference..., credential;`), so if iteration 1 sets credential and iteration 2's lookup fails, iteration 2 reuses iteration 1's credential — updating the WRONG calendar with the wrong credential. This is a real bug: the credential variable must be scoped inside the loop (const per iteration).

findings.title: Shared `credential` variable across loop iterations in updateAllCalendarEvents causes cross-reference credential leakage
findings.body: `credential` is declared once outside the `for (const reference of calendarReference)` loop (line 480: `let calendarReference: PartialReference[] | undefined = undefined, credential;`). Inside the loop (lines 511-542), when `reference.credentialId` is set, credential is assigned from this.calendarCredentials or DB. If a reference has no credentialId (else branch, line 543-550), credential is NOT reassigned — but the else branch uses a local `credentials` variable, so that's fine. However, if the credentialId branch's DB lookup fails (credentialFromDB null), credential retains the PREVIOUS iteration's value, and `updateEvent(credential, ...)` at line 542 uses the wrong credential for the current reference — updating a calendar event on the wrong user's calendar with the wrong credentials. This can modify another user's calendar event (data integrity/security issue). Fix: declare `let credential` inside the loop body (per-reference scope), and skip/throw when the credential cannot be resolved.

findings.title: Sequential await in destination loop creates calendar events one-by-one, slow for collective events with many hosts
findings.body: createAllCalendarEvents iterates `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` with `await createEvent(...)` inside (lines 339-383), making calendar event creation sequential per destination. For collective events with N hosts, this serializes N external API calls. The previous code used Promise.all for the no-credentialId branch. The credentialId branch also does a potential DB fetch per destination (line 344). This is a performance regression for collective events — should use Promise.all over destinations (with per-destination credential resolution). Severity medium since collective events typically have few hosts, but with the DB fetch inside the loop it's N sequential round trips.

findings.title: Team members' destination calendars collected via users.slice(1) but users ordering/host assignment for ROUND_ROBIN may include unbooked hosts
findings.body: teamDestinationCalendars is built from `users.slice(1)` — all users except the first. For COLLECTIVE, all users attend, so this is correct. But `users` comes from loadUsers which for hosts-based event types returns `eventType.hosts.map(...)` — ALL hosts, not just available/booked ones. For COLLECTIVE, ensureAvailableUsers filters to available users before this point? The teamMemberPromises at line ~990 uses `users` — need to verify `users` at that point is the filtered available users (after ensureAvailableUsers). Looking at the flow: ensureAvailableUsers returns availableUsers, and `users` is reassigned? The diff context doesn't show the reassignment. If `users` still contains all hosts (not just available ones), then for a collective event where only 2 of 3 hosts are available, the third host's destinationCalendar would be included and EventManager would try to create a calendar event on their calendar using their credential — but the EventManager is constructed with only the organizer's credentials (`new EventManager(organizerUser)` or similar), so createAllCalendarEvents' DB fallback (line 344) would fetch the third host's credential from DB and create an event on their calendar even though they're not part of the booking. This would be wrong. Need to verify that `users` at line 990 is the availability-filtered list. The variable `users` is declared earlier and ensureAvailableUsers is called with users — the result should be assigned back. If not, this is a bug. Given the diff shows `const teamMemberPromises = users.slice(1).map(...)` without visible reassignment of users after ensureAvailableUsers in the shown context, this is suspicious. At minimum, the code should use the same filtered user list used to build attendees/teamMembers.

findings.title: buildUIDCalendarEvent has inverted guard: throws when users exist instead of when they don't
findings.body: Line 179-181: `if (this.users && this.users.length > 0) { throw new Error("call buildUsers before calling this function"); }`. The error message says "call buildUsers BEFORE calling this function", but the condition throws when users ARE present — the guard is inverted. It should be `if (!this.users || this.users.length === 0)`. As written, buildUIDCalendarEvent throws whenever users have been set (the correct precondition), and proceeds to `const [mainOrganizer] = this.users` (line 182) when users is undefined — which would throw a different error (Cannot read properties of undefined). This is a pre-existing bug (not introduced by this PR — the diff only shows the import change), but it's in a changed file and the PR touches this builder's destinationCalendar handling. Worth fixing while here, but since it's pre-existing and unrelated to the destinationCalendar change, severity is low.

findings.title: Inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED conditionals break organization slug assignment
findings.body: The diff changed `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` and `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { requestedSlug: slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {})`. The first change is a semantic inversion: previously, when team billing was NOT enabled, the slug was set directly on the organization; now it's only set when billing IS enabled. The second change is equivalent (&& → ternary). The first change alters behavior: with IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED=false (self-hosted default), organizations no longer get their slug set at creation — `slug` will be null, breaking organization subdomain routing. This looks like an accidental inversion unrelated to the destinationCalendar PR (possibly a bad merge or drive-by change). It must be reverted to `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` or justified. This is a critical regression for self-hosted org creation.

findings.title: evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) mutates the array that may be shared with eventType.destinationCalendar or organizerUser.destinationCalendar
findings.body: Line ~1060-1064: `destinationCalendar: eventType.destinationCalendar ? [eventType.destinationCalendar] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [organizerUser.destinationCalendar] : null` — this creates a NEW array containing the Prisma object, so pushing to it (line 1074: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`) does not mutate the Prisma objects themselves, only the new array. So no shared-state mutation of Prisma results. However, the array now contains a mix of the eventType/organizer destination and team members' destinations — when persisted (line ~1871), only [0] is connected. Already reported. Additionally, if the same DestinationCalendar object appears twice (e.g. two hosts share the same destination calendar row — unlikely since destinationCalendar is per-user), duplicates could cause duplicate event creation in createAllCalendarEvents (the loop doesn't dedupe by credentialId). Low risk. Not reporting separately — covered by the persistence finding.

findings.title: MeetLocationType fallback check uses mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration but DestinationCalendar.integration is the app slug like 'google_calendar' — verify field semantics
findings.body: Line 119: `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")`. The Prisma DestinationCalendar model has an `integration` field (string) — its values are app slugs like "google_calendar", "office365_calendar". The check `!== "google_calendar"` is correct for detecting absence of Google Calendar. But when destinationCalendar is empty (now common — many call sites pass []), mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and `.integration` throws (already reported as the crash finding). The fix `?.integration` would make the condition true (undefined !== "google_calendar") → falls back to Cal Video, which is the correct behavior for no Google Calendar. So the optional chaining fix is correct and necessary.

findings.title: BrokenIntegrationEmail calendar name parsing can produce 'undefined undefined' or wrong name when destinationCalendar is empty
findings.body: Line 88-96: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = calEvent.destinationCalendar ?? []; let calendar = mainHostDestinationCalendar ? mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration.split("_") : "calendar"; if (Array.isArray(calendar)) { const calendarCap = calendar.map(...); calendar = calendarCap[0] + " " + calendarCap[1]; }`. If integration is e.g. "google_calendar", split gives ["google","calendar"], calendarCap[0]="Google", calendarCap[1]="Calendar" → "Google Calendar" — OK. But if integration has only one segment (e.g. "caldav"), calendarCap[1] is undefined → "Caldav undefined". If integration is undefined (destination entry without integration), split throws. Pre-existing fragility, now more likely because destinationCalendar entries may be partial. Low severity since this email is only sent on broken integrations (and the send is currently commented out in CalendarManager).

findings.title: Google Calendar hangoutLink patch uses selectedCalendar which may be undefined, causing patch to target wrong calendar
findings.body: In createEvent, after insert, if the event has a hangoutLink, the code calls `calendar.events.patch({ calendarId: selectedCalendar, ... })` (line 166-177). selectedCalendar is `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` — which is undefined when no destination matches the credential (line 147-149), even though the insert used `selectedCalendar || "primary"` (line 154). So the patch targets calendarId=undefined while the insert went to "primary" — the patch will fail (Google API error) or hit the wrong calendar, leaving the event description without the Meet link. The patch should use `selectedCalendar || "primary"` consistently. Same pattern in updateEvent (line 277: `calendarId: selectedCalendar` where selectedCalendar could be undefined when externalCalendarId is falsy and the find fails — see the broken find at line 254-256).

findings.title: Booking destinationCalendar connect uses evt.destinationCalendar[0].id — but for collective events the first entry may be a team member's calendar if organizer has none
findings.body: Line ~1871-1877: `destinationCalendar: evt.destinationCalendar && evt.destinationCalendar.length > 0 ? { connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id } } : undefined`. evt.destinationCalendar[0] is eventType.destinationCalendar or organizerUser.destinationCalendar (the organizer's), and team members' calendars are appended after. So [0] is the organizer's — correct for the primary. But if the organizer has NO destination calendar and eventType has none, evt.destinationCalendar starts as null and teamDestinationCalendars are pushed only if `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)` — wait, line 1074: `if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE") { evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars); }` — if evt.destinationCalendar is null (no organizer/eventType calendar), the push is skipped (optional chaining), so team members' calendars are NOT included! For a collective event where the organizer has no destination calendar but team members do, the event would only be created on... createAllCalendarEvents: destinationCalendar is null → else branch → broken fallback (filter type === "calendar") → no events created, OR if the fallback worked, only one. The team members' calendars are silently dropped because the push is conditional on evt.destinationCalendar being non-null. Fix: initialize evt.destinationCalendar to [] and push team calendars unconditionally for collective, or build the array as [...(organizer ? [organizer] : []), ...teamDestinationCalendars].

findings.title: Collective team destination calendars are dropped when organizer has no destination calendar (null?.push no-op)
findings.body: Line ~1060: `destinationCalendar: eventType.destinationCalendar ? [eventType.destinationCalendar] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [organizerUser.destinationCalendar] : null`. Line ~1074: `if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE") { evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars); }`. When neither eventType nor organizerUser has a destinationCalendar, evt.destinationCalendar is null, and `null?.push(...)` is a no-op — the team members' destination calendars (collected in teamDestinationCalendars at line ~990) are silently discarded. EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents then sees destinationCalendar as null/empty and falls into the broken fallback branch (filter `cred.type === "calendar"` matches nothing), so NO calendar events are created for any host — the booking exists but no one gets a calendar invite. This is a regression for collective events where the organizer lacks a destination calendar but hosts have them. Fix: build the array as `[...(eventType.destinationCalendar ? [eventType.destinationCalendar] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [organizerUser.destinationCalendar] : []), ...(isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE" ? teamDestinationCalendars : [])]`.

findings.title: Fallback branch credential filter `cred.type === "calendar"` never matches; should be endsWith("_calendar") excluding other_calendar
findings.body: Line 389: `const [credential] = this.calendarCredentials.filter((cred) => cred.type === "calendar");`. No credential has type exactly "calendar" — types are "google_calendar", "office365_calendar", "apple_calendar", "caldav_calendar", etc. This fallback (used when event.destinationCalendar is empty/null) therefore never creates a calendar event. With the PR making empty arrays the norm (many call sites now pass [] instead of a populated object), bookings for users WITHOUT a configured destination calendar will get NO calendar event created — a silent regression. The filter should be `cred.type.endsWith("_calendar") && !cred.type.includes("other_calendar")` (other_calendar is handled separately below at line 402), or simply pick the first calendar credential.

findings.title: Cancellation iterates all calendar references but uses bookingToDelete.user.credentials (organizer only) — team hosts' credentials fetched from DB individually, but recurring branch uses all user credentials indiscriminately
findings.body: The non-recurring branch (lines 422-483) correctly resolves each reference's credentialId against bookingToDelete.user.credentials first, then falls back to a DB fetch (lines 428-441) — good, this handles team hosts whose credentials aren't in bookingToDelete.user.credentials. But the recurring branch (lines 444-468) ignores the reference's credentialId entirely: it iterates ALL of `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` filtered by `type.endsWith("_calendar")` and for each, deletes the first `_calendar` reference found in each updated booking. For collective recurring events, references belong to different hosts' credentials; using the organizer's credentials to delete events on other hosts' calendars will fail (404, silently resolved) leaving orphaned events. The recurring branch should use the same per-reference credential resolution as the non-recurring branch.

findings.title: Calendar interface createEvent signature change (added credentialId) is a breaking change for third-party/custom calendar app implementations
findings.body: The `Calendar` interface's createEvent was changed from `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` to `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)`. TypeScript allows implementations with fewer parameters, so existing implementations compile, but the semantic contract changed: implementations that don't use credentialId will create events on the wrong calendar for collective events (as detailed in the BaseCalendarService/Office365/Lark findings). For app-store apps shipped in this repo, the implementations should be updated. For any external/custom apps (Cal.com supports custom apps via the app store structure), this is a behavioral breaking change. The PR should update ALL in-repo implementations (BaseCalendarService, Office365, Lark — currently not updated) to accept and honor credentialId.

findings.title: updateLocation referencesToCreate uses result.externalId/credentialId which are not populated by CalendarManager.updateEvent
findings.body: In updateLocation (lines 201-211), referencesToCreate maps `externalCalendarId: result.externalId, credentialId: result.credentialId ?? undefined`. But CalendarManager.updateEvent (lines 272-323) does NOT set externalId or credentialId on its returned EventResult — looking at the return object (lines 313-322), it returns appName, type, success, uid, updatedEvent, originalEvent, calError, calWarnings — no externalId, no credentialId. So result.externalId and result.credentialId are always undefined here, and the references created by updateLocation will have externalCalendarId undefined and credentialId undefined. Previously the code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId` and `result.credentialId ?? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId` — also mostly undefined for the array case. The consequence: after a location change (editLocation.handler), the booking's references are recreated (prisma.booking.update with references: { create: updatedResult.referencesToCreate }) — wait, editLocation.handler line 119-121 does `references: { create: updatedResult.referencesToCreate }` — this ADDS new references without deleting old ones? Actually it creates new references alongside existing ones. The new references lack externalCalendarId/credentialId, so future updates/deletes (which rely on reference.credentialId and reference.externalCalendarId) will not find the right calendar — updateAllCalendarEvents falls to the else branch (filter by type) and deleteEvent gets externalCalendarId undefined. This breaks subsequent reschedule/cancel for the booking. CalendarManager.updateEvent should populate externalId (from the externalCalendarId param) and credentialId (from credential.id) in its return value.

findings.title: updateEvent does not return externalId/credentialId in EventResult, breaking reference tracking for location updates
findings.body: CalendarManager.updateEvent (lines 272-323) returns an EventResult without `externalId` or `credentialId` fields, even though it receives `externalCalendarId` and `credential` as parameters. EventManager.updateLocation builds referencesToCreate from `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId` (EventManager.ts lines 208-209), which are therefore always undefined. The references persisted after a location change (editLocation.handler.ts line 119-121: `references: { create: updatedResult.referencesToCreate }`) will lack externalCalendarId and credentialId. Subsequent reschedule/cancel operations rely on these fields (EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents line 505-509 reads reference.externalCalendarId; handleCancelBooking reads reference.credentialId) — with them missing, updates fall back to type-based credential matching (may pick wrong credential for users with multiple calendar apps) and deletes get externalCalendarId undefined (hitting the broken fallback paths). Fix: add `externalId: externalCalendarId, credentialId: credential.id` to updateEvent's return object.

findings.title: Location update creates new booking references without deleting old ones, causing duplicate references
findings.body: Line 113-123: `prisma.booking.update({ where: { id: bookingId }, data: { location, references: { create: updatedResult.referencesToCreate } } })`. This CREATES new references but does not delete the existing ones. After a location change, the booking will have both old references (with old uids/externalCalendarIds) and new references. EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents filters references by type and iterates ALL of them — so subsequent reschedule/cancel will attempt to update/delete BOTH the old and new calendar events, causing errors (old event may already be deleted or belong to a different location's video meeting) and potentially updating stale calendar entries. The old references should be deleted first (or use upsert). This may be pre-existing behavior (the diff doesn't show changes to this logic), but combined with the new externalId/credentialId population issues, it's worth flagging. Actually checking the diff — this file's only change is the destinationCalendar array wrapping. So the duplicate-reference issue is pre-existing. Downgrade to low/speculative? The PR's changes to EventManager.updateLocation (externalId/credentialId now from result, which are undefined) make the newly created references LESS useful than before (previously they carried evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId). So the PR regresses this path. Keep as medium with focus on the regression.

findings.title: isTeamEventType check changed from enum comparison to string array includes — verify SchedulingType import and values
findings.body: Line ~689: changed from `eventType.schedulingType === SchedulingType.COLLECTIVE || eventType.schedulingType === SchedulingType.ROUND_ROBIN` to `!!eventType.schedulingType && ["COLLECTIVE", "ROUND_ROBIN"].includes(eventType.schedulingType)`. The string literals must match the Prisma enum values exactly. SchedulingType enum in Prisma is COLLECTIVE, ROUND_ROBIN, MANAGED. The string comparison works if eventType.schedulingType is the enum string. But the import of SchedulingType may now be unused (check). Also, the CalendarEvent type now includes `schedulingType?: SchedulingType | null` (added in Calendar.d.ts line 182) and handleNewBooking sets `schedulingType: eventType.schedulingType` on evt (line ~1071) — this is a new field in the webhook payload. This is an additive change, fine. The isTeamEventType change is semantically equivalent. Low severity — just verify no unused import lint error and that the enum values match.

findings.title: EventManagerUser type still has destinationCalendar: DestinationCalendar | null (singular) but the class no longer uses it
findings.body: Line 62-65: `export type EventManagerUser = { credentials: CredentialPayload[]; destinationCalendar: DestinationCalendar | null; };`. The constructor (lines 78-87) only uses user.credentials — destinationCalendar is not used. Callers construct EventManager with `{ ...user, credentials }` where user may have destinationCalendar (singular, from Prisma). This type is now misleading since CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar is an array. The EventManagerUser type should either drop destinationCalendar or change to DestinationCalendar[]. Since it's unused in the constructor, dropping it would be cleanest, but callers pass it — TypeScript allows extra properties in spread. Low severity (type hygiene), but could confuse future maintainers.

findings.title: Organizer email overridden with mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId (calendar ID, not email) for Google Calendar events
findings.body: Lines 122-124 (createEvent) and 228-230 (updateEvent): `email: mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId ? mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId : calEventRaw.organizer.email`. For Google Calendar, externalId IS the calendar ID which for primary calendars is the user's email, but for secondary calendars it's a calendar ID (like abc123@group.calendar.google.com), not an email. Setting the organizer attendee's email to a calendar ID is invalid — Google may reject the event or misattribute the organizer. This was pre-existing behavior (the old code did `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.externalId ? calEventRaw.destinationCalendar.externalId : calEventRaw.organizer.email`), so not a regression, but it's wrong and now more impactful because destinationCalendar is an array and the first entry may be a secondary calendar. The organizer email should remain calEventRaw.organizer.email; the calendar selection is handled by calendarId. This is a pre-existing bug worth fixing but not introduced by this PR — low severity in the context of this review.

findings.title: teamDestinationCalendars collected from users.slice(1) but for collective events the organizer is users[0] — verify users[0] is always the organizer/booking user
findings.body: Line ~990: `const teamMemberPromises = users.slice(1).map(async (user) => { if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE" && user.destinationCalendar) { teamDestinationCalendars.push(user.destinationCalendar); } ... })`. This assumes users[0] is the organizer (whose destinationCalendar is used as the primary at line ~1060 via organizerUser.destinationCalendar). But `organizerUser` is a separate variable — is it guaranteed to be users[0]? For collective events, users comes from eventType.hosts or eventType.users. The organizerUser is determined elsewhere (likely the event type owner or the first user). If organizerUser !== users[0], then users.slice(1) might include the organizer (duplicate) or exclude a team member. Also, for collective events, ALL users attend, so all their destination calendars should be included — but the code excludes users[0] from teamDestinationCalendars and uses organizerUser.destinationCalendar as primary. If users[0] !== organizerUser, the organizer's calendar might be pushed as a team member AND used as primary (duplicate), or users[0]'s calendar is dropped. Need to verify organizerUser === users[0]. The diff doesn't show organizerUser assignment. This is a potential correctness issue for collective events — flagging for verification.

findings.title: createAllCalendarEvents mixes sequential and parallel creation; DB credential fetch inside loop is a bottleneck and potential N+1
findings.body: The destination loop (lines 339-383) is sequential (`for...of` with `await`), and inside it, when the credential isn't in this.calendarCredentials, a `prisma.credential.findUnique` DB query is executed (line 344) — one query per destination per booking creation. For collective events with many hosts whose credentials aren't pre-loaded, this is N sequential DB round trips + N sequential external API calls. The credentials could be batch-fetched with `findMany({ where: { id: { in: destinationCredentialIds } } })` before the loop, and event creation parallelized with Promise.all. Performance issue for collective bookings — medium severity.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation inner loop shadows `uid` and `externalCalendarId` from outer reference destructuring
findings.body: Lines 423-424: `const { credentialId, uid, externalCalendarId } = reference;` (outer scope). Lines 453-456: inside the recurring branch, `const bookingRef = updBooking.references.find(...); if (bookingRef) { const { uid, externalCalendarId } = bookingRef; ... }` — the inner destructuring shadows the outer uid/externalCalendarId. This is intentional (using the per-booking reference's uid), but the shadowing is confusing and error-prone. More importantly, the inner loop uses `calendar` from the OUTER credential (the reference's credential), iterating over ALL user calendar credentials in the outer `promises` map (line 449-461: `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).map(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... })`) — wait, re-reading: the recurring branch is INSIDE the `if (calendarCredential)` block (line 442), and the `promises` map at line 449 iterates `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` (ALL calendar credentials), creating a calendar service for each and deleting the bookingRef's event with EACH credential. So for a recurring booking with 2 calendar credentials, each updated booking's event is deleted twice (once per credential) — the second delete will 404 (silently resolved in Google). For collective recurring events, the reference belongs to a specific host's credential, but deletion is attempted with ALL of the organizer's credentials — wrong credentials will fail, and if the organizer has a credential of the same type as the host, it might delete from the wrong calendar (if externalCalendarId matches, which it won't across users). The net effect: redundant API calls and potential confusion, but the correct credential's delete should succeed. The logic should use the specific `calendar` (from calendarCredential) rather than iterating all user credentials. This is the same issue as finding #18 but worth emphasizing the shadowing and the all-credentials iteration.

findings.title: Merge-delete of old calendar event uses getCalendar(calendarCredential) which may be null, then optional-chains deleteEvent — silently skips deletion
findings.body: Lines 553-565: when newBookingId is provided (merge scenario), the old calendar event is deleted: `const calendarCredential = await prisma.credential.findUnique(...); const calendar = await getCalendar(calendarCredential); await calendar?.deleteEvent(...)`. If calendarCredential is null (deleted credential) or getCalendar returns null (unknown app type), `calendar?.deleteEvent` is a no-op — the old calendar event is silently left on the user's calendar. This is pre-existing behavior (the diff shows this block was moved but not fundamentally changed). Low severity — silent failure, but pre-existing.

findings.title: Duplicate destination calendars not deduplicated — same calendar pushed twice creates duplicate events
findings.body: If two collective hosts share the same destination calendar (same DestinationCalendar row — possible if they share a team calendar or the same credential+externalId), teamDestinationCalendars will contain duplicates, and evt.destinationCalendar will have duplicate entries. EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents iterates destinations and calls createEvent per destination — for entries with the same credentialId, two events are created on the same calendar (duplicate calendar events). The loop should dedupe by credentialId (or externalId+integration). Medium severity — edge case but real for teams sharing calendars.

findings.title: Lark updateEvent error path calls deleteEvent(eventId, event) without calendarId, which will throw 'no calendar id'
findings.body: Line 224-228: in updateEvent's catch block, `await this.deleteEvent(eventId, event)` is called without the third `externalCalendarId` argument. deleteEvent (line 236-242) computes `calendarId = externalCalendarId || mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` — if the event has no destinationCalendar (or the first entry has no externalId), it throws "no calendar id provided in deleteEvent". So the error-recovery path (delete the partially-updated event) will itself throw, masking the original error. The catch should pass the resolved calendarId: `await this.deleteEvent(eventId, event, calendarId)`. Pre-existing pattern but exposed by the array change.

findings.title: PayPal webhook evt.destinationCalendar doesn't include team hosts' calendars for collective paid events
findings.body: Line 152-156: `destinationCalendar: booking.destinationCalendar ? [booking.destinationCalendar] : user.destinationCalendar ? [user.destinationCalendar] : []`. For collective paid events, this only includes the booking's (first) destination calendar. When EventManager.create is called (line 170) for an already-confirmed booking, createAllCalendarEvents will only create events for this single destination — team hosts' calendars are not included, so hosts won't get calendar events when a paid collective booking is confirmed via PayPal webhook. The booking.destinationCalendar only stores the first destination (per the persistence finding). This means the PayPal confirmation path creates fewer calendar events than the initial booking path. For Stripe (webhook.ts handlePaymentSuccess, line 229), same issue. These webhook paths reconstruct evt from the booking and lose the multi-destination information. Since booking.destinationCalendar is a single relation, the information is lost at persistence time — the webhook handlers cannot recover it. This is a consequence of the schema limitation (single destinationCalendar on Booking). High-level issue: paid collective bookings confirmed via webhook will not create calendar events on all hosts' calendars.

findings.title: Stripe webhook evt.destinationCalendar doesn't include team hosts' calendars for collective paid events
findings.body: Same issue as PayPal webhook: line 229 `destinationCalendar: selectedDestinationCalendar ? [selectedDestinationCalendar] : []` where selectedDestinationCalendar is booking.destinationCalendar || user.destinationCalendar (single). For collective paid events confirmed via Stripe webhook, EventManager.create (line 243) will only create calendar events for this single destination — team hosts' calendars are excluded. Combined with the booking persistence storing only the first destination, the webhook confirmation path cannot create events on all hosts' calendars. This is a data-model limitation exposed by the PR's multi-destination feature.

findings.title: confirm.handler evt.destinationCalendar doesn't include team hosts' calendars for collective bookings requiring confirmation
findings.body: Line 175-179: `destinationCalendar: booking?.destinationCalendar ? [booking.destinationCalendar] : user.destinationCalendar ? [user.destinationCalendar] : []`. When a collective booking requiring confirmation is confirmed (line 225: handleConfirmation → EventManager.create), the evt only has the booking's single destination calendar. Team hosts' calendars are not included, so handleConfirmation's EventManager.create will only create calendar events for the organizer's calendar — hosts won't receive calendar invites when the booking is confirmed. The booking.destinationCalendar stores only the first destination (per persistence finding), and the confirm handler doesn't have access to the original multi-destination array. This is a functional gap for collective + requiresConfirmation flows: hosts are added as attendees (via evt.team?) but their calendars don't get events. Actually, handleConfirmation calls EventManager.create which uses evt.destinationCalendar — with only one entry, only one calendar event is created. The other hosts are in evt.team.members (if set) and would be invited as attendees to the organizer's calendar event, but won't have the event on their own calendars. This matches the PR's goal ("host can get invited correctly") — invited as attendees, yes, but not getting their own calendar event. Depending on interpretation, this may be acceptable (hosts get the event via attendee invitation on the organizer's calendar), but the PR title says "handle collective multiple host on destinationCalendar" implying each host's calendar should get the event. The confirm path doesn't achieve that.

findings.title: TypeError when destinationCalendar is empty array: mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration on undefined
findings.body: Line 118-119: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []; if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")`. When evt.destinationCalendar is `[]` (now produced by many call sites: bookingReminder.ts:130, webhook.ts:119/229, confirm.handler.ts:175-179, editLocation.handler.ts:85-89, requestReschedule.handler.ts:240-242, deleteCredential.handler.ts:290-294, handleCancelBooking.ts:251-255/528-532, paypal-webhook.ts:152-156), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined`, and `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`. This crashes EventManager.create for ANY Google Meet booking where destinationCalendar is empty — i.e., users without a configured destination calendar who use Google Meet. The optional chaining `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` is required; with it, undefined !== "google_calendar" is true, correctly falling back to Cal Video.

findings.title: CalendarEventClass.destinationCalendar type uses Prisma DestinationCalendar[] but CalendarEvent interface allows null — class should match
findings.body: Line 26: `destinationCalendar?: DestinationCalendar[] | null;` — matches the interface. OK, no issue. Skip.

findings.title: bookingReminder evt.destinationCalendar uses booking.destinationCalendar || user.destinationCalendar — single calendar, no team hosts
findings.body: Line 107: `const selectedDestinationCalendar = booking.destinationCalendar || user.destinationCalendar;` and line 130: `destinationCalendar: selectedDestinationCalendar ? [selectedDestinationCalendar] : []`. This is only used for sendOrganizerRequestReminderEmail (line 133) — an email, not calendar event creation. So the destinationCalendar in the evt is only used for email content (if at all). Low impact — the reminder email doesn't create calendar events. No fix needed beyond consistency.

findings.title: evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) — optional chaining on possibly-null array silently skips team calendars
findings.body: Line ~1074: `if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE") { evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars); }`. When evt.destinationCalendar is null (no eventType.destinationCalendar and no organizerUser.destinationCalendar — line ~1063 sets null in that case), the `?.push` is a no-op and teamDestinationCalendars are silently dropped. This means collective events where the organizer has no destination calendar configured will not create calendar events on team members' calendars either — the entire multi-host destination feature is defeated in this case. The array should be initialized to include team calendars regardless: `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]` for collective events.

findings.title: createEvent in no-credentialId branch doesn't pass destination.externalId, losing calendar selection for Google
findings.body: Line 376-382: when a destination entry has no credentialId, the code finds all credentials matching `destination.integration` and calls `createEvent(c, event)` — WITHOUT passing `destination.externalId` as the third argument. CalendarManager.createEvent's third param `externalId` is then undefined, and the returned EventResult.externalId is undefined. GoogleCalendarService.createEvent uses `credentialId` (second param, correctly passed as `credential.id` by CalendarManager) to find the matching destination calendar — so for Google, the calendar selection still works via credentialId matching. BUT the returned reference's externalCalendarId will be undefined (since result.externalId is undefined), so future updates/deletes that rely on reference.externalCalendarId will fall back to the (broken) destinationCalendar lookup. The call should be `createEvent(c, event, destination.externalId)` to thread the externalId through.

findings.title: createEvent's externalId parameter is optional but GoogleCalendarService relies on credentialId matching — inconsistent selection mechanisms
findings.body: CalendarManager.createEvent (line 218-270) accepts `externalId?: string` and passes it through to the result. GoogleCalendarService.createEvent (line 87) accepts `credentialId: number` and uses `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` — it does NOT use the externalId param passed by CalendarManager (CalendarManager doesn't even pass externalId to calendar.createEvent — it only puts it in the result!). Wait, let me re-read: CalendarManager.createEvent line 236: `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` — it passes credential.id as the second arg (credentialId), NOT externalId. The externalId param of CalendarManager.createEvent is only used in the return value (line 267: `externalId`). So GoogleCalendarService receives credentialId and finds the destination by credentialId — correct. But the externalId param of CalendarManager.createEvent (passed by EventManager as destination.externalId) is IGNORED by the calendar service — it's only recorded in the result. For Google, credentialId matching works. For other services that don't use credentialId (Office365, CalDAV, Lark — which don't even accept the param), the externalId is not used for calendar selection. So the externalId param is effectively dead for calendar selection — it's only metadata. This is a design inconsistency: either services should accept and use externalId for selection, or the param should be removed. Currently, Google works via credentialId; others are broken for multi-destination (as reported).

findings.title: Only first destination calendar persisted on booking — multi-host destination info lost for reschedule/cancel/confirm flows
findings.body: Line ~1871-1877: `destinationCalendar: evt.destinationCalendar && evt.destinationCalendar.length > 0 ? { connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id } } : undefined`. The Booking Prisma model has a single `destinationCalendar` relation (one-to-one). The evt.destinationCalendar array contains the organizer's calendar plus all collective team members' calendars (built at lines ~1060-1074). Only the FIRST entry's id is connected to the booking. All subsequent flows that reconstruct evt.destinationCalendar from the booking (handleCancelBooking line 251-255, confirm.handler line 175-179, requestReschedule.handler line 240-242, editLocation.handler line 85-89, payment webhooks) will only see the organizer's calendar — team hosts' destination calendars are lost. While calendar event updates/deletes primarily use booking.references (which do capture all created events with their credentialIds), the destinationCalendar-based fallbacks in calendar services and the evt passed to emails/webhooks will be incomplete. For the PR's stated goal ("host can get invited correctly"), the critical paths (create) work via references, but reschedule/cancel rely on references too (EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents iterates references). The main risk is the broken fallback paths in GoogleCalendarService (update/delete find by externalId) and the evt.destinationCalendar used for email content. A proper fix requires a schema migration to support multiple destination calendars on Booking (many-to-many), or ensuring all flows rely exclusively on references (which have credentialId + externalCalendarId per event).
